name: oes-partner-pipeline
narrative: Zara runs supply for Komadugu Health Initiative, which operates eleven therapeutic feeding sites across Borno. They know their caseload precisely, because they admit the children — and today they know almost nothing about the supply they depend on. This is that inverted. Inbound consignments arrive in the frame Komadugu actually plans in: a distribution day, at a named site, with a known number of children expected, each one reading as covered, at risk, or uncovered. From what has physically arrived and the rate they are admitting, each site shows its weeks of cover and the date it runs dry — the difference between planning and triaging admissions. When a truck arrives short, the storekeeper counts it and records the receipt themselves, and the shortfall becomes a discrepancy raised by the person holding the cartons rather than an argument between head offices. When cover will not last, Zara raises a shortfall signal from this screen, and it lands in the OES command centre as the exception their team acts on. And because Komadugu's own workers already screen every child they treat, a received batch can be followed forward — to the distributions it fed, and to one child's arm circumference climbing out of the red.

zara.name: Zara Mustapha
zara.intro: Zara plans distributions for eleven therapeutic feeding sites and is the person who decides, when supply is short, which site gets what. Today they learn a consignment is late when the truck fails to arrive, find out what was really in it by counting cartons on a loading bay, and report a shortfall by telephoning someone in Abuja. Their own organisation is the only one touching both the carton and the child, and it is the one with no instrument to show it.

slides.title: The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
slides.narration: Everything a central team sees looks outward. Turn it around. Komadugu Health Initiative runs eleven feeding sites in Borno. They know their caseload to the child, because they are the ones admitting them — and they know almost nothing about the supply they depend on. They learn a consignment is late when a truck does not arrive. They find out what was in it by counting cartons on a loading bay. And they report a shortfall by telephone. They are also the only organisation in this entire chain that touches both the carton and the child, which makes them the one positioned to prove the supply chain worked, and the one with no instrument to do it.

slides.title: Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
slides.narration: A shipment table sorted by arrival date is a supplier's view of the world. Zara's unit of planning is a distribution day, at a named site, with a known number of children expected — so that is the frame the inbound supply is shown in. Next Tuesday at Monguno needs eight hundred cartons for the children booked in; the consignment covering it is on the road and reads as covered. The Thursday distribution at Kukawa reads as at risk, and the one after it has nothing assigned to it at all. That is information Zara can act on, in the shape they already think in.

slides.title: Weeks of cover, and the date it runs dry
slides.narration: From what has physically arrived and the rate they are admitting children, every site shows two numbers: how many weeks of cover it is holding, and the date it runs dry. This is the figure that changes behaviour. At four weeks of cover you plan. At one week you start triaging admissions, which is a decision nobody wants to make quickly or quietly. Kukawa is eleven days out. Knowing that three weeks early is the entire point, and no partner in this sector currently gets it as a live number.

slides.title: The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
slides.narration: When the truck reaches Monguno, the storekeeper counts what came off it and records the receipt from a phone. The advice said nine hundred cartons; eight hundred and forty arrived. That difference becomes a discrepancy the moment it is recorded, and it is raised by the person standing next to the pallets. A shortfall asserted from a capital city is a dispute. The same shortfall recorded at the loading bay against the despatch advice is evidence — and it is labelled as hand-keyed, because it was.

slides.title: Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
slides.narration: Kukawa will not last. Zara raises a shortfall from this screen: the site, the date, the children affected, the cartons short. It does not go into a message queue somebody may or may not read — it lands in the OES command centre ranked against every other exception by the children behind it, and marked as raised by Komadugu rather than derived centrally. The direction is what matters here: the ground reporting upward into a system that can respond, rather than the centre reporting downward about the ground. What OES does with it is the next narrative.

slides.title: From a batch to the child who recovered
slides.narration: Komadugu's own workers already screen every child they treat, and that record and the supply record have never been the same chain. Joined up, they are. Zara opens a batch that arrived last month and follows it forward — to the distributions it supplied, to the children admitted on it, and to one child whose arm circumference climbs across their visits out of red, through yellow, into green. Recovered. This is the linkage the funding standards describe and the sector achieves as far as the contract and then abandons. The last mile here is synthetic and says so; the point is that both ends of it already exist and can be held as one record.
